title: Two parallel host LLM resolvers (runtime.wiring and applications._shared) with divergent routing semantics; owner doc names only resolve_llm_adapter()
affected_invariant: FRZ-OWN-03 one sanctioned composition owner / FRZ-OWN-05 no duplicated semantic mechanism (LLM provider selection and routing composition)
impact: Two modules each define resolve_llm_adapter / evaluate_llm_routing / consume_routing_evaluation and each keeps its own module-global _last_routing_evaluation. The Tier-3 variant (applications/_shared) adds live model-routing wiring (resolve_live_model_routing_wiring) and wrap_routing_evaluating_adapter; the runtime/wiring variant builds only create_adapter / create_adapter_with_failover and has no capability check or routing-evaluating wrapper. The same application (local_workspace_application) imports both: host/agent_factories.py uses applications._shared, serving/workspace_routes.py and workspaces/ask_service.py use runtime.wiring. An LLM adapter materialized through the second path therefore skips live routing evaluation and the routing-evaluation record read by the first. LLM_ADAPTERS.md (L482, L602) names resolve_llm_adapter() without a module, so the owner doc does not decide between them. EBH-2E (CLOSED) certifies 'one owner of concerns' for the LLM boundary.
recommendation: Owner decision: declare one sanctioned host resolver (or make one delegate to the other), name it in LLM_ADAPTERS.md, and add a gate that rejects a second resolve_llm_adapter definition. Campaign B should execute both paths with routing_profile set to confirm the behavioral difference.

title: Plane C vision adapters fabricate a 0.99-confidence 'object.stub' detection when the backend is unconfigured or returns zero detections
affected_invariant: FRZ-CFG-02 (missing configuration cannot silently select a vendor/backend; fail closed or explicitly disabled) / FRZ-CFG-06
impact: TritonVisionInferenceAdapter and HuggingFaceInferenceVisionAdapter delegate to StubVisionInferenceAdapter in two cases: (a) no URL / API key configured (silent substitution of a configured-by-slug provider) and (b) the real backend answered successfully but parsing produced zero detections. The stub returns a full-frame bbox with label 'object.stub' and confidence 0.99 inside an ordinary VisionInferenceResult, so a consumer cannot tell a fabricated result from a real one; case (b) turns 'nothing detected' into a false positive. The behavior is documented (MODALITY.md L320-321, L376) as 'stub fallback', which makes it an accepted design choice, but it contradicts the FRZ-CFG-02/06 text (both PASS under CONFIG-X). HuggingFace host and default model id (api-inference.huggingface.co, facebook/detr-resnet-50) are also literals in the adapter (L31, L54), relevant to FRZ-CFG-05. Not executed (E3 = code at SHA only).
recommendation: Owner decision: either fail closed (typed unconfigured error) / mark results with an explicit stub provenance flag, or document the stub fallback as harness-only and make it unreachable from production profiles. Campaign B: confirm whether any production profile can select slug vision_serving / huggingface_inference without the env variable.

title: Direct ollama SDK use outside the provider boundary (Tier-0 multimedia, Tier-2 qualifier); agent vendor-import gates do not list ollama and LLM_ADAPTERS dimension 3 is stated as 'Yes'
affected_invariant: FRZ-CTR-02 concrete provider leakage = 0; LLM_ADAPTERS M-LLM-R dimension 3 'Vendor SDK only inside providers/*'
impact: intergrax/multimedia/images_loader.py imports the ollama SDK at module level and calls ollama.chat directly (default model 'llava-llama3:latest'); image_smart_loader._caption_via_ollama routes Plane B image captioning through it for Ollama adapters instead of LLMAdapter. agents/model_routing_qualifier/qualification_types.py imports ollama.ResponseError at L149. Both Tier-2 gate scripts omit ollama from their banned lists (check_agents_vendor_imports: openai, boto3, httpx, slack_sdk, google.cloud, azure; check_agents_no_vendor_sdk_imports: openai, anthropic, boto3, torch, ...), although native Ollama is the documented default local provider, so the agent-side import is invisible to the gate. LLM_ADAPTERS.md L573 nonetheless records 'Vendor SDK only inside providers/*' as Yes citing check_agents_vendor_imports.py. Scale is small (3 call sites) but it contradicts a closed-stage conformance statement.
recommendation: Route image captioning through LLMAdapter (describe_image / multimodal messages) or move it behind a provider module; add ollama and the other LLM SDK roots (anthropic, google.genai, mistralai, cohere, ollama) to both agent gate scripts and add a Tier-0 gate for intergrax/ outside llm_adapters/providers and rag/embedding/providers.

title: Silent vendor/backend defaults when unconfigured: embedding provider -> ollama, vector store -> in-memory, notification backend -> log (invalid value also -> log); CONFIG-X scan has a blind spot for vendor-slug defaults
affected_invariant: FRZ-CFG-02 / FRZ-CFG-06 / FRZ-CFG-08 (CONFIG-X, all PASS in checklist)
impact: (1) create_default_embedding_manager() with no env/profile resolves slug 'ollama' (provider_authority.py L15/L19, resolver.py L82) - the LLM path in the same program fails closed with LLMProviderNotConfiguredError (runtime/wiring/llm_resolver.py L47). (2) create_vectorstore_from_integration falls back to the in-memory store when no vector_store slug is configured (L107, L120), although RAG.md L510 classifies InMemory as 'harness use only'. (3) resolve_notification_settings maps an unset OR unparsable backend to NotificationBackend.LOG (L44-49) and create_notification_adapter ends with a LOG fallback (factory.py L98), so a mistyped production backend silently degrades to log-only. The CONFIG-X semantic scan (_classify_resolved_semantic_string_default) only flags tenant_id 'default' and localhost URLs; every other string default, including provider='ollama', is classed APPROVED_TYPED_CONFIGURATION, and the concern inventory lists llm.embedding as class A. FRZ-CFG-02/06/08 are PASS with 'silent fallback' gates, so the gate coverage does not reach these three selectors. Capacity (runtime/capacity/production_adapters.py L80-90: in-memory Kubernetes scaler when INTERGRAX_KUBERNETES_URL is unset) is a fourth instance for the C18 batch. Not executed; documented in docstrings, which is why this is MEDIUM and not HIGH.
recommendation: Owner decision per selector: fail closed or explicit 'disabled'/'harness' mode; extend the CONFIG-X scan to vendor-slug string defaults and add a negative test per selector. Campaign B: confirm production composition always passes an explicit embedding/vector/notification choice.

title: Concrete integration providers are imported and selected by enum/string switches in Tier-1 runtime and Tier-3 application code, beside IntegrationProfile resolution
affected_invariant: FRZ-CTR-02 concrete provider leakage = 0 / FRZ-PLG-04 provider selection has explicit owner / FRZ-BND-05
impact: git grep at the SHA (line-start imports of intergrax.integrations.providers.*) finds 65 files under intergrax/runtime (43 of them in runtime/vendor_knowledge; the rest include notifications/factory.py, transport/bootstrap.py, capacity/production_adapters.py, long_running/*, human/store.py, events/store.py), 16 non-script/non-test files in applications/local_workspace_application (kafka/redis bundles, jira/confluence/google/msgraph integrations), plus rag, collaborative_work, autonomous_work, queueing and others. Several are enum/string switches that pick a provider bundle directly (NotificationBackend, config.backend == 'kafka'/'rabbitmq'), i.e. a second provider-selection mechanism next to IntegrationProfile / resolve_from_profile. This is the same class as the filed agents/* finding EQOA-A4-004 but outside agents/; no gate was found that covers runtime/ or applications/ (check_agents_vendor_imports scans agents/ only). Some imports are only sqlite path constants (events/store.py L11) and vendor_knowledge is a by-design provider-contribution area, so the count overstates real bypasses; the switch factories are the substantive part. FRZ-CTR-02/PLG-04 are OPEN in the checklist, so this is consistent with the checklist state and is reported as scope evidence, not as drift.
recommendation: Owner decision: sanction provider-bundle imports only inside named composition roots and register them in a gate allowlist, or move the switches behind IntegrationProfile resolution. Campaign B: classify the 65+16 files into sanctioned composition, constant-only and bypass.

title: MCP_SERVER.md architecture/plan header says 'stage not CLOSED, P6 in progress' while the roadmap records MCP-SERVER-X CLOSED (published, scoped)
affected_invariant: Documentation canon currency (roadmap decides stage status)
impact: The feature architecture doc (last touched 2026-11-11 by the P6 commit 5ff8606b0) still states 'P2-P5 engine scoped; P6 DX in progress (T-IGX-035-G) - stage not CLOSED' and lists 'Planned logical components'; roadmap L570 states MCP-SERVER-X = CLOSED - INDEPENDENTLY AUDITED (INTERNAL AGENT CERTIFICATION) - PUBLISHED (SCOPED). Roadmap is the deciding authority, so the closure stands and the doc is stale; a reader of the owner doc would conclude the opposite. The MCP engine itself sits in intergrax/applications/_shared/mcp_*.py (a Tier-0 package named 'applications'), which is also where EQOA-A4-003 applies.
recommendation: Owner updates the status line and component wording of the feature architecture and plan docs to the closed state.

title: Owner-doc coverage gaps in concern C05-C09 packages: runtime/llm, runtime/plugins, capability_acquisition, capability_qualification and the 16-module marketplace-qualified tool execution path
affected_invariant: FRZ-OWN-01 every major concern has exactly one semantic owner
impact: The package census records no canonical architecture-doc mention for intergrax/runtime/llm, runtime/plugins, capability_acquisition and capability_qualification (unowned_candidate). The qualified-marketplace tool execution path occupies 16 top-level modules in intergrax/tools (marketplace_*, qualified_marketplace_*) and is described only in maintainers/architecture/S24_GAP_02_QUALIFIED_MARKETPLACE_TOOL_HANDOFF.md and qualification records, not in TOOLS.md, CAPABILITY_MARKETPLACE_ENGINE.md or their satellites (git grep over docs/project/architecture and docs/project/capabilities returned nothing). PLATFORM_PLUGINS.md does mention RuntimePlugin at L369 but not the runtime/plugins package. E2: absence established by grep, content roles taken from module heads.
recommendation: Owners add the packages/paths to the canonical owner docs or record a maintainers-doc as the owner.
